events.title: The death of Pope St. Dionysius
events.shortBlurb: The pope who gathered up the wreck of the Valerianic persecution and judged the great Dionysius of Alexandria died in the last days of 268…
body: A presbyter of the Roman Church under Pope Stephen, Dionysius had taken part in the controversy over heretical baptism, and Dionysius of Alexandria wrote to him as to an excellent and learned man. After the martyrdom of Sixtus II on 6 August 258, the violence of the persecution left the Roman See vacant nearly a year, until on 22 July 259 Dionysius was raised to it.

Some months later the emperor Gallienus issued his edict of toleration, which brought the persecution to an end and restored to the Church its buildings for worship, its cemeteries, and other properties; the new pope brought its administration once more into order. He is counted the first Bishop of Rome not to suffer martyrdom.

About 260 his Alexandrian namesake, writing against Sabellianism, expressed himself with inexactness concerning the Logos; the accusation was laid before the pope, who called a synod at Rome and issued, in his own name and the council's, a doctrinal letter condemning alike the error of Sabellius and the new error that separated the divine monarchy into three. He died on 26 December 268, as the greater number of authorities reckon; some give 27 December.
